claims.text: SPS can produce single-phase ZrB2 from compacted ZrB2 powder at approximately 1800 °C with a dwell time below 10 minutes.
The proposed SPS route will produce significantly lower porosity than conventional sintering above 2300 °C.
The proposed SPS route will enhance the mechanical integrity of single-phase ZrB2.
Reduced porosity and enhanced integrity will lower the probability of hole formation and failure during prolonged liquid plating-bath exposure.
SPS of the powder can be performed under uniaxial pressure and vacuum or inert atmosphere using pulsed electric current.
A pressure of approximately 50 MPa is appropriate for the proposed ZrB2 SPS process.
A molybdenum-foil liner with an additional graphite-paper layer will ensure uniform heating and prevent contamination.
The relevant SPS preparation window is 1800–2000 °C, a heating rate around 100 °C/min, and a dwell time below 10 minutes.
The proposed process controls will restrict thermal gradients and shorten high-temperature exposure.
Localized Joule heating and applied pressure promote rapid neck formation and densification during SPS.
Short, intense SPS prevents excessive grain growth and pore coarsening in ZrB2.
The proposed SPS route yields a refined, uniform, and nearly fully dense ZrB2 microstructure.
Pulsed electric current and applied pressure lower kinetic barriers for mass transport, enabling densification at reduced temperature.
Rapid sintering minimizes the time available for pore nucleation and pore growth.
A denser ZrB2 microstructure is more resistant to erosive degradation in prolonged liquid plating-bath service.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 sintered above 2300 °C has higher porosity and greater microstructural inhomogeneity.
Porosity and microstructural inhomogeneity in conventionally prepared ZrB2 predispose it to hole formation and eventual component failure.
Thermal and chemical stresses during extended liquid plating-bath exposure can exacerbate porosity-related defects.
The SPS material is predicted to have lower porosity, greater mechanical strength, and a more uniform microstructure than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
The degree of porosity reduction, mechanical improvement, densification uniformity, and long-term plating-bath performance remains uncertain and requires experimental quantification.
